normalized.governing_thought: Onsoo should enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, not national retail, and fund it step by step against hard gates
executive_summary: Answer: yes, enter the US in 2027 with the Amazon-led route (Option A), run as a gated programme. It is the only route that stays inside the board's cash and margin guardrails. Retail-led breaks them on its own numbers, and a Japan scale-up is safe but builds no US business.

The US is worth entering now: the category is growing fast and Onsoo's products already sell there. US K-beauty skincare grew 17% a year to $3.6B (2021–25), five times faster than the rest of facial skincare. In the Amazon pilot, monthly units nearly doubled in six months (7,400 → 14,000) at 4.5 stars, and 90-day repeat (29%) is close to the 31% benchmark.

Amazon-led is the only route that fits the guardrails; retail-led fails all three financial tests. Option A's cumulative cash bottoms at −$1.9M to −$3.9M against the $18M cap, and group margin stays at 9.0% or more. Option B bottoms at −$20.8M even on its own assumptions, cuts group margin to 4.5% in 2027, and rests on sell-through and halo assumptions the evidence contradicts. Japan adds just $7M of revenue by 2030.

The binding risk is ad cost: payback by 2030 needs ACoS of 28.6% or less. No route reaches $40M by 2030. The pilot ran at 28% ACoS, but brands scaling from $5M to $20M have a median of 32%. At 32%, Option A is still −$2.3M at end-2030 and payback slips past 2030. The worst tested case costs $6.4M, about a third of the cap. Option A reaches $26.4M in 2030 and about $40M by 2032.

Approve Option A with hard gates, re-phase the ambition, and replace the 2029 retail trigger. Fund a $4M peak-cash envelope and review at end-2027 against ACoS ≤28%, revenue ≥$7M and repeat ≥31%. Consider retail only when aided awareness is above 20% and a right-sized plan fits the guardrails. A national retail launch in 2029 would cut group margin to 6.0%.

slides.title: We tested the CEO's hypothesis against seven conditions: the Amazon launch holds up, but the 2029 retail step and the 2030 target do not

claims.claim: Starting hypothesis (CEO): “Launch in the US in 2027 through Amazon, then add specialty beauty retail from 2029 once Amazon sales pass $10M and aided awareness passes 15%.”
1. The US market is large and growing for K-beauty skincare — HOLDS
evidence: $3.6B in 2025, up 17% a year since 2021, against 3.5% a year for other facial skincare

claims.claim: 2. Onsoo's products sell in the US — HOLDS
evidence: Pilot: 64,800 units ($1.56M) in six months; 4.5 stars from 2,140 reviews; repeat 29% vs 31% benchmark

claims.claim: 3. Amazon-led stays inside the cash cap and margin floor — HOLDS
evidence: Peak cash −$1.9M to −$3.9M across plan and evidence-based cases (cap −$18M); group margin ≥9.0%

claims.claim: 4. Amazon-led pays back by end-2030 — AT RISK
evidence: Only if ACoS averages ≤28.6% (≤26.9% if duty rises to 25%); pilot 28%, scaling benchmark 32%

claims.claim: 5. Amazon-led beats the alternatives — HOLDS
evidence: Retail-led fails the cap, payback and margin floor; Japan adds $7M revenue in a market growing 1.5% a year

claims.claim: 6. Retail can be added in 2029 at >$10M Amazon sales and >15% awareness — FAILS
evidence: At 10–20% awareness, newcomers sell 3.5 units/door/week (delisting bar 4.0); national retail in 2029 cuts group margin to 6.0%

claims.claim: 7. The chosen route reaches $40M revenue by 2030 — FAILS
evidence: No route does within the guardrails: A reaches $26.4M; B reaches $37.6M but burns $20.8M

claims.claim: Revised answer: Keep the 2027 Amazon-led launch. Treat 2030 payback as at risk and manage to an ACoS gate. Replace the 2029 retail trigger: aided awareness above 20%, plus a retail plan that fits the guardrails. Re-phase the $40M ambition to about 2032.

slides.title: Retail-led's gap is structural: no plausible sell-through or halo pays back $7.5M a year of retail fixed cost by 2030

claims.claim: Option B peak cumulative cash 2027–30 by sell-through and halo (1.0× / 1.3× plan / 1.6× / 2.0×)
Cost: retail adds $7.5M a year of fixed cost, plus a $0.5M launch fee and $0.66–1.1M of fixtures.
Contribution: retail units earn only $1.1–1.8M a year even at the plan's 4.5 units/door/week, so the layer loses about $6M a year before any halo.
Halo needed: about 1.6× Option A's Amazon volume just to fit the cap, and about 3.1× to pay back by 2030. The plan assumes 1.3×, with no causal evidence (p. 11).
Margin: B's 2027 US operating loss of $8.7M is 2.6 times the $3.3M the group can absorb while holding 8%. This fails in every case.

Every cell fails the payback test (cumulative cash below zero at end-2030) and the 8% group-margin floor in 2027. Even top-quartile sell-through with double the Amazon halo leaves B $11.6M short of payback.

slides.title: A Japan scale-up is safe but small: +$7M revenue and +$1.8M cash by 2030 in a market growing 1.5% a year

claims.claim: Option J · Japan scale-up, $M (2027–30)
Safe: J passes every financial guardrail, with peak cash of −$1.05M and group margin of at least 10.1%.
Small: $7M is 4% of group revenue by 2030, in a market growing about 1.5% a year where Onsoo already holds 3.1%.
Off-strategy: it builds nothing towards the board's US ambition, and the pilot's momentum and learning would sit idle for a year.

slides.title: Payback by 2030 hinges on advertising efficiency: Amazon-led pays back only if ACoS averages 28.6% or less, about the pilot's level

claims.claim: Hurdle: ACoS ≤ 28.6%; ≤ 26.9% if the duty rises to 25%
evidence: Option A cumulative cash end-2030, $M (duty 15% / 25%): ACoS 25% plan 2.4 / 1.3; ACoS 26% benchmark low 1.7 / 0.6; ACoS 28% pilot 0.4 / −0.7; ACoS 32% benchmark median −2.3 / −3.4; ACoS 38% benchmark high −6.4 / −7.5 (pairing as extracted)

Each ACoS point = $0.67M of cumulative cash by 2030
So what: treat 2030 payback as at risk. Manage ACoS to 28% or below as a gate, and expect payback to slip beyond 2030 if ACoS tracks the benchmark. The cap and margin floor still hold.

slides.title: Model approach: all inputs come from the briefing pack; where it was silent we made the choices below and flag them

claims.claim: How the numbers are built
evidence: Amazon contribution/unit = $24 − 15% referral − $5.10 FBA − $3.50 ex-factory − $0.55 freight − 15% duty on ex-factory − ACoS × $24
Retail contribution/unit = $14 wholesale − $3.50 − $0.75 freight − duty − 8% co-op − 4% returns = $7.545
Retail units = doors × units/door/week × 52; Option B Amazon units = Option A × halo
Cash flow = contribution − fixed costs − one-time costs − inventory build
Inventory = four months of landed cost (ex-factory + freight + duty) on each year's units
Group margin = (11.0% × ex-US revenue + US operating profit) ÷ (ex-US + US revenue)
Payback test: cumulative US cash ≥ 0 by end-2030. Cap test: most negative cumulative cash ≥ −$18M
Breakeven ACoS: the average ACoS at which Option A's end-2030 cumulative cash is exactly zero (solved numerically)

claims.claim: Choices made where the pack is silent
evidence: “On the way to $40M by 2030” read as $40M revenue in 2030 (p. 15 shows both readings)
Inventory is built in the year volume is sold and not released by 2030; this is conservative for every option
One-time costs (set-up, launch fee, fixtures) are expensed, so they also count in the margin test
New doors sell for the full year they are added, which flatters Option B
Evidence-based ACoS = 32%, the agency median for brands scaling from $5M to $20M; 28% (pilot) shown as the middle case
Onsoo awareness read as below 10% on Table 8's basis: 4% of all buyers, 9% of K-beauty buyers
Option J excludes working capital, which the pack does not give; this flatters J slightly
No discounting, inflation or price changes; FX at KRW 1,380 per $ (only as context)
Stall case: 200k units a year (≈$4.8M, the level of the Amazon-first peers below $5M) at 28% ACoS

normalized.recommendation: Approve Option A: Amazon-led US entry in 2027; do not launch national specialty retail in 2027. Fund a $4M peak-cash envelope through Gate 2; re-phase the ambition to “$25M+ in 2030, on the way to $40M by about 2032”, keeping the cash, payback and margin guardrails; replace the retail trigger with aided awareness >20%, Amazon ≥$20M and a retail plan that fits the guardrails (instead of >$10M and >15% in 2029); defer Japan, don't drop it — bring the Japan scale-up back in the 2028 plan. Let three gates (Gate 1 end-2027, Gate 2 end-2028, retail trigger 2029 or later), not the calendar, release each further step and each further dollar.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Chosen. The only route that stays inside the board's cash and margin guardrails; passes the cap and margin floor in every case; payback by 2030 holds at 25–28% ACoS but not at the 32% benchmark.

Rejected. Fails every financial guardrail even on its own numbers (peak cash −$20.8M, group margin 4.5% in 2027); −$31.1M on evidence; rests on sell-through and halo assumptions the evidence contradicts; gap is structural.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Deferred, not dropped. Safe (passes every guardrail) but small (+$7M revenue by 2030 in a market growing 1.5% a year) and off-strategy; can return in the 2028 plan as the bandwidth limit applies to 2027 only.

alternatives_considered.option: CEO hypothesis: add specialty retail from 2029 once Amazon sales pass $10M and aided awareness passes 15%

alternatives_considered.option: Keep $40M in 2030 and relax the guardrails
alternatives_considered.treatment: Not recommended. Means accepting at least $21M of peak cash (above the cap), group margin below 8% for three years, and Mooncrest-type risk; even then B's own plan reaches $37.6M, not $40M. Recommended instead: keep the guardrails, re-phase the ambition.

alternatives_considered.option: Retail via a limited door test rather than 600 national doors
alternatives_considered.treatment: Proposed for 2029 or later if the retail trigger is met ("Start with a right-sized test, not 600 national doors"); to be costed by the planning team in 2028.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Evidence base: the planning-team briefing pack only (no outside research). All company, competitor and market figures in the pack are synthetic benchmark data.
The binding risk is ad cost: payback by 2030 needs ACoS of 28.6% or less (≤26.9% if duty rises to 25%); pilot 28% on a small budget, scaling benchmark 32% (26–38%).
Plan ACoS of 25% assumes ACoS falls as the brand matures; nothing in the pack supports this.
Launch stall risk: two of three Amazon-first peers stayed below $5M US revenue; stall case −$6.3M by 2030.
Pilot growth is slowing: +16–17% a month to +8–9%.
US tariff review (15% → 25%), decision expected mid-2027: about −$1.1M by 2030.
FX: product costs are in won; 10% weaker won about +$1.1M by 2030 (stronger won the reverse); treated as a swing factor.
Repeat purchase (29% vs 31% benchmark) not modelled separately; underpins the volume path.
6% of reviews cite Korean-only labels; MoCRA registration required.
“On the way to $40M by 2030” read as $40M revenue in 2030; if the board meant only a trajectory, Option A already satisfies it.
Inventory is built in the year volume is sold and not released by 2030; conservative for every option.
One-time costs are expensed, so they also count in the margin test.
New doors sell for the full year they are added, which flatters Option B.
Evidence-based ACoS = 32%; 28% (pilot) shown as the middle case.
Onsoo awareness read as below 10% on Table 8's basis: 4% of all buyers, 9% of K-beauty buyers.
Option J excludes working capital, which the pack does not give; this flatters J slightly.
No discounting, inflation or price changes; FX at KRW 1,380 per $ (only as context).
Hero-SKU economics applied to all SKUs, as the planning team does.
2031–32 is an illustrative extension at 23% a year, not a forecast.
Option B evidence case is before / ignores the likely delisting at the 12-month review.
Halo: the 0.71 doors–Amazon correlation does not show causation; plan's 1.3× halo has no causal evidence.
